title: Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
notes: Cover date December 2000; the DCI's foreword is dated 13 December 2000. Second edition, December 2000. Scope: dated or quantified projections the NIC states in its own voice in the Overview (pp. 5-18), then the four 'Alternative Global Futures' scenarios (appendix, pp. 83-84), in print order (the PDF text layer puts Scenario Two before Scenario One, so entries are ordered by the printed scenario numbers, not by text position). The 'Discussion' chapters and regional sections were not mined. Horizon 2015 has passed. Read from the Wayback copy of the original cia.gov file; the current dni.gov copy blocks scripts and its URL was not confirmed.

entries.label: Over three billion people in water-stressed regions
entries.quote: the over three billion individuals who will be living in water-stressed regions from North China to Africa
entries.subject: water scarcity

entries.label: World population 7.2 billion in 2015
entries.quote: World population in 2015 will be 7.2 billion, up from 6.1 billion in the year 2000, and in most countries, people will live longer.
entries.subject: world population

entries.label: 95 percent of population increase in developing countries
entries.quote: Ninety-five percent of the increase will be in developing countries, nearly all in rapidly expanding urban areas.
entries.subject: world population
entries.metric: share of 2000-2015 population increase in developing countries

entries.label: Food production adequate; malnourishment in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa
entries.quote: Overall food production will be adequate to feed the world’s growing population, but poor infrastructure and distribution, political instability, and chronic poverty will lead to malnourishment in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa.
entries.subject: food security

entries.label: Energy demand up 50 percent; resources sufficient
entries.quote: Despite a 50 percent increase in global energy demand, energy resources will be sufficient to meet demand
entries.subject: energy demand
entries.note: Overview. Base year not stated (2000 implied).

entries.label: Regional tensions over water heightened by 2015
entries.quote: Regional tensions over water will be heightened by 2015.
entries.subject: water scarcity
entries.note: Overview. Regions named: Middle East, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, northern China.

entries.label: Global growth returns to 1960s-early 1970s levels
entries.quote: The global economy, overall, will return to the high levels of growth reached in the 1960s and early 1970s.
entries.subject: global economic growth
entries.note: Overview. The text adds that a sustained financial crisis or energy disruption 'could undo this optimistic projection'.

entries.label: Russia, China, North Korea, Iran, Iraq able to strike the US
entries.quote: Russia, China, most likely North Korea, probably Iran, and possibly Iraq have the capability to strike the United States
entries.subject: nuclear weapons
entries.note: Overview, Future Conflict: 'Strategic WMD threats, including nuclear missile threats, in which (barring significant political or economic changes)...'. Graded likelihood per country: most likely, probably, possibly.

entries.label: Low risk of war among developed countries
entries.quote: The risk of war among developed countries will be low.
entries.subject: great power conflict

entries.label: Internal conflicts stay at current levels or increase
entries.quote: Internal conflicts stemming from religious, ethnic, economic or political disputes will remain at current levels or even increase in number.
entries.subject: internal conflict

entries.label: Rising likelihood of WMD use against the US
entries.quote: The likelihood will increase over this period that WMD will be used either against the United States or its forces, facilities, and interests overseas.
entries.subject: weapons of mass destruction

entries.label: US influence unparalleled in 2015
entries.quote: US global economic, technological, military, and diplomatic influence will be unparalleled among nations as well as regional and international organizations in 2015.
entries.subject: US global role
entries.note: Overview, Role of the United States.

entries.label: Europe and Japan need 110 million new workers by 2015
entries.quote: European and Japanese populations are aging rapidly, requiring more than 110 million new workers by 2015 to maintain current dependency ratios between the working population and retirees.
entries.subject: population aging
entries.metric: new workers needed in Europe and Japan to hold dependency ratios
entries.note: Overview, Key Uncertainties: Global Economy. A requirement, not a forecast of what happens; low gradability.

entries.label: Russia remains internally weak
entries.quote: The most likely outcome is a Russia that remains internally weak and institutionally linked to the international system primarily through its permanent seat on the UN Security Council.
entries.subject: Russia

entries.label: India's population 1.2 billion by 2015
entries.quote: The size of its population—1.2 billion by 2015—and its technologically driven economic growth virtually dictate that India will be a rising regional power.
entries.subject: India
entries.note: Overview, Key Uncertainties: India. The Discussion chapter says 'more than 1.2 billion'.

entries.label: Inclusive Globalization
entries.quote: A virtuous circle develops among technology, economic growth, demographic factors, and effective governance, which enables a majority of the world’s people to benefit from globalization.
entries.subject: globalization

entries.label: Pernicious Globalization
entries.quote: Global elites thrive, but the majority of the world’s population fails to benefit from globalization.
entries.subject: globalization
entries.note: Appendix, Scenario Two, p. 83. The global economy splits into three; WMD used in at least one internal conflict.

entries.label: Regional Competition
entries.quote: Regional identities sharpen in Europe, Asia, and the Americas, driven by growing political resistance in Europe and East Asia to US global preponderance and US-driven globalization and each region’s increasing preoccupation with its own economic and political priorities.
entries.subject: global order

entries.label: Post-Polar World
entries.quote: US domestic preoccupation increases as the US economy slows, then stagnates.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Appendix, Scenario Four, p. 84. US-European alliance deteriorates, US withdraws troops from Korea and Japan, Asian rivalries escalate toward a China-Japan crisis.
